Title (copy for cal): Lightning Talk: Prediction-Action Markets for Coordination
Description: Non-risk-neutral agents can use prediction markets to hedge against undesired outcomes.  If the aggregate preferences result in the market cap exceeding the cost of intervention, the prediction market becomes an action market incentivizing the aggregate desired world.  This dynamic can be used as a coordination mechanism, assuming market bids always resolve, but this turns out to work less well for risk-averse agents than for risk-seeking agents.  Such dynamics can be concretely probed with toy examples such as the prisoner's dilemma, exposing the assumptions that underpin "libertarian utopias".
